author: Josh Butler
description:
Defence confirmed the fatality occurred on Monday at the Mount Bundey training area, with next of kin informed

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

An Australian soldier has died and five others were injured in a training accident at a facility outside Darwin yesterday, according to the defence department.

The department on Tuesday morning released a statement confirming the incident, which occurred at the Mount Bundey training area, around 100km south-east of Darwin in the Northern Territory.
title: Australian soldier killed and five others injured in training exercise in the Northern Territory

author: Raphael Rashid in Seoul
description:
Exclusive: Guardian analysis finds more than 150,000 tonnes of fuel was shipped to Russian ports in July and August, some using sanctioned tankers

Oil is being shipped from South Korea to Russia via sanctioned tankers as Moscow scrambles for supplies amid the war in Ukraine, a move one expert said “undermines” Seoul’s public backing for Kyiv.

Guardian analysis of port records and ship-tracking data found that in July and August over 176,000 tonnes of fuel, mostly diesel, was loaded at several South Korean ports on to seven tankers that made 14 voyages to Russia’s far east.

Continue reading...
title: Oil from South Korea being shipped to Russia as Ukraine war grinds on

author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
Sources say the opposition’s target will be below Labor’s but won’t match One Nation’s goal to limit net arrivals to 130,000

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

The Coalition is expected to reveal deep cuts to immigration today which the party says would maintain working holidaymaker places and prioritise skills as part of attempts to dent growing support for One Nation.

The opposition leader, Angus Taylor, is expected to unveil the Coalition’s policy on Tuesday, after signoff from Liberal and National MPs in a special party room meeting due t
title: Coalition set to unveil dramatically deeper cuts to overseas migration as it fends off One Nation’s rise

author: Cecilia Nowell and Guardian staff
description:
President says ‘I’m doing great’ despite polls showing 32% approval rating and loss of support from 2024 voters

Donald Trump’s approval ratings reached a record low on Monday, according to new opinion polls.

A new Reuters/Ipsos poll shows Trump’s approval rating at a record-low 32%. That polling included the president losing support among independent voters and Latinos, who had backed him in 2024. The dip could prove dire for the Republican party a month ahead of the midterm elections that will determine control of Congress.

Continue reading...
title: Trump approval ratings plummet to new low, polls show

author: Sam Levin and agencies
description:
Shavdon Gayden killed Eddimar Hernandez-Chacon in broad daylight while walking with her older sister

A woman has been charged with murder after allegedly stabbing a seven-year-old girl, with police describing it as an unprovoked attack on a sidewalk in Chicago.

Shavon Gayden, 48, has been charged with one count of first-degree murder, Chicago police said in a statement on Sunday. The killing happened just before noon on Saturday in the Chatham neighborhood. The victim has been identified by local media and the medical examiner’s office as Eddimar Hernandez-Chacon.

Continue reading...
title: Woman charged with murder after stabbing seven-year-old girl in Chicago

author: Guardian Staff
description:
Neighboring states are also reporting hundreds of cases, with over 3,800 recorded across the country

Pennsylvania has surpassed 1,000 measles cases this year, state health officials calculate, making it the largest state outbreak in more than three decades. The benchmark comes as neighboring New York declared a state of emergency about measles rates there.

Pennsylvania’s health department said Monday 1,004 cases of measles had been confirmed. Five Pennsylvania residents ⁠have died ⁠after ​contracting the disease, with 198 hospitalizations.

Continue reading...
title: Pennsylvania faces largest measles outbreak in decades as case count rises to 1,000

author: Jessica Elgot and Dan Sabbagh
description:
Party to unveil plans for one of UK’s ‘most significant military programmes since the cold war’

The Conservatives will announce plans to build a £10bn British “Iron Dome” similar to Israel’s air and missile defence system, which the party will christen “Britannia Shield” in an announcement at conference on Tuesday.

The shadow defence secretary, James Cartlidge, will say Britain needs to be ready to defend itself from potential aerial attacks and that new investment was needed in advanced radar and interceptor missiles.

Continue reading...
title: Conservatives propose £10bn ‘Britannia Shield’ inspired by Israel’s Iron Dome

author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
Government push comes as part of major offensive launched under air cover by Saudi military coalition, aiming to retake all territory held by Houthis

Forces of the Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen have recaptured several key areas around Bab el-Mandeb Strait from Iran-backed Houthi rebels, Yemeni officials said Monday.

The officials said forces allied with the internationally recognized government have retaken the crucial town of Dhubab just north of the strait. They also captured the towns of Bab and Hadeid, said the officials, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to reporters. Witnesses said they saw government tanks and forces entering the towns.

Continue reading...
title: Saudi-backed forces recapture key areas around strait from Houthis in Yemen

author: Dani Anguiano
description:
Hilton faces heavy backlash from within his own party for ‘Just Try It’ ad amid his longshot bid for California governor

Steve Hilton, the Republican candidate for California governor, is receiving heavy criticism from members of his own party over a controversial, sexual innuendo-filled campaign ad that has been described as “creepy”.

The video entitled “Just Try It, California” was released last week and depicts two young women with brightly colored hair, sitting on a bed in front of a pride flag in low lighting. One nervously says “I can’t believe I’m doing this”, while another strokes her hair and coaxes “don’t be nervous, it’s not that bad” before guiding her to fill out a ballot for Hilton and aggressively commanding “lick it”.

Continue reading...
title: Republicans criticize Steve Hilton for ‘creepy’ innuendo-filled campaign ad

author: Tom Phillips in Rio de Janeiro
description:
Experts say strength of evangelical church and stubbornness of Lula, 80, also helped propel Jair Bolsonaro’s son to first-round election win

On Sunday night, as the scale of the far-right triumph in Brazil sank in, an adapted football chant rang out in one of Rio’s most leftwing areas.

“Let’s turn this around, Lu-laaaaa! Let’s turn this around, Lu-laaaaa! Let’s turn this around, Lu-laaaaa!” crestfallen progressives bellowed while drowning their sorrows after witnessing an excruciating election setback for their leader, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

Continue reading...
title: Far right on the march and Lula’s failures: key drivers of Flávio Bolsonaro’s Brazil surge

author: Victoria Bekiempis
description:
PepsiCo initiated class II recall of 28oz bottles last month over ‘undeclared’ yellow dyes, FDA notice says

About 122,000 cases of the popular sports drink Gatorade have been voluntarily recalled across 37 US states due to their having “undeclared” food dye, according to an official federal notice.

The varieties of the drink involved in the notice include 28oz bottles of Gatorade Lemon Lime, Lime Zero, Orange and Gatorade Orange Zero, the notice said. Gatorade’s manufacturer – the soda giant PepsiCo – initiated its recall on 25 September, said the advisory, which was posted on the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA)’s website.

Continue reading...<
title: Gatorade maker recalls 122,000 cases of popular sports drink across 37 US states

author: Victoria Bekiempis
description:
Authorities say crash in Winter Haven involved three vehicles, including bus filled with dozens of high schoolers

A high school student and one other person were killed in a crash that caused a school bus to flip over on to its roof in central Florida early on Monday, according to authorities.

About 26 students traveling on the public school bus involved in the crash were taken to the hospital, the Polk county sheriff’s office said in a statement posted to Facebook. The bus had 39 occupants: 37 high school students, the bus driver and the driver’s daughter, officials said.

Continue reading...
title: Florida high schooler and one other killed in school bus rollover crash

author: Ariana Baio
description:
‘I don’t control message or what we’re doing,’ scandal- hit state attorney general reportedly says at private event

Ken Paxton, the Texas attorney general chosen by Donald Trump to run as the Republican candidate for a Senate seat, admitted in private that his campaign was being controlled by outside forces in Washington DC.

Paxton, who is locked in a competitive race with the progressive Democrat James Talarico, told people at a fundraising event in September that he had never felt such little control over his campaign because of outside influence.

Continue reading...
title: Republican Ken Paxton admits forces in DC control his Texas Senate campaign

author: Presented by Lucy Houghwith Dan Sabbagh; produced by Angus Neale; senior producer Ryan Ramgobin; executive producer Zoe Hitch
description:
The US withdrew its bombers from RAF Fairford after an investigation into an alleged planned terrorist attack on the base. At least 10 B-1 bombers used by the US military in the Iran conflict flew out of Fairford on Sunday, suggesting US officials were taking the threat seriously. Last week, five men in three vans near the military base were arrested, followed by a sixth British-Iranian national. All were released on bail, drawing criticism from the Pentagon.

Lucy Hough speaks to Dan Sabbagh, the Guardian’s defence and security editor – watch on YouTube

Continue reading...
title: Why did the US rush to withdraw bombers from RAF Fairford? - The Latest

author: Associated Press
description:
The Republican, who was sent to prison in 2016 in a hush-money case tied to the allegations, died over the weekend

Dennis Hastert, the longest-serving Republican US House speaker, died over the weekend, a coroner said Monday. He was 84.

Hastert, who was speaker from 1999 until 2007, died of natural causes at his home, according to Jacquie Purcell, the Kendall county coroner.

Continue reading...
title: Dennis Hastert, former House speaker disgraced by molestation allegations, dies aged 84

author: Victoria Bekiempis
description:
Texas tops list with 8,100 bans while Stephen King is again most banned author, PEN America finds

The US saw almost 12,000 book bans in public schools during the 2025-2026 school year, the highest number in a single year, according to the free-expression non-profit PEN America.

In a report released on Monday, PEN America said that there had been 34,000 instances of book bans since the organization started tallying the increasing “book censorship crisis” across US schools in 2021.

Continue reading...
title: US book bans in public schools reach record annual high of 12,000

author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
description:
Departure comes amid large drop in oil receipts, rampant inflation and shrinking economy

Iran’s oil minister has resigned days after allegations that an intermediary trust selling Iranian oil abroad owed millions of dollars’ worth of export receipts to the state.

Mohsen Paknejad’s departure comes as Iran grapples with a dire economic situation, including inflation running at 85%. An overall drop in oil receipts has led to a massive shortfall in foreign exchange earnings and one of the biggest drops in the value of the rial since the Iranian revolution in 1979.

Continue reading...
title: Iran’s oil minister resigns as country’s economic crisis worsens

author: Chris Osuh
description:
Public figures back commissioner’s call for government commitment to funding legal support for those affected

The singer and television personality Mel B has said she is “heartbroken” by the Windrush scandal victims’ fight for justice, as the Windrush commissioner urged ministers to commit to providing funding for legal support for those affected by the end of October.

In April, the Guardian revealed that the Home Office had refused to pay compensation in more than half the claims made by victims of the scandal, in which mainly Black Britons who came legally to postwar Britain were wrongly stripped of citizenship and settlement rights.

Continue reading...
title: Mel B ‘heartbroken’ by Windrush scandal victims’ fight for justice

author: Christopher Knaus and Ariel Bogle
description:
Exclusive: Guardian Australia investigation reveals state governments use shared graves to bury those deemed too poor to pay for funerals. ‘It’s unspeakable,’ one relative says

  • Find more from the Unmarked graves investigation here

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Vietnam veterans, rough sleepers and other impoverished Australians are being buried in unmarked communal graves often holding four or more people, a practice relatives have described as “unspeakable” and “a disgrace”.

A Guardian Australia investigation has identified more than 100 unmarked graves across New South Wales, and some in Queensland, that
title: Hundreds of Australians, including war veterans, are being buried in unmarked communal graves

author: Luca Ittimani
description:
Peak Jewish bodies organise ceremonies on third anniversary of attacks that triggered conflict in which 74,000 Palestinians have been killed

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Jewish Australians will mark the third anniversary of the 7 October attacks on Wednesday as Labor state governments condemn pro-Palestinian vigils to be held the same day.

Peak Jewish bodies have organised commemorations across the capital cities but avoided publicising locations as community members report ongoing fears for their safety since the Bondi terror attack in December.
title: Australian leaders condemn pro-Palestine vigils planned for 7 October anniversary amid Jewish commemorations

author: Josh Butler
description:
Unions, employer groups, banks and industry experts will appear at the four-day hearings along with OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft and Google

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

OpenAI must explain how they will stop their models from inappropriately accessing Australian data, the Labor chair of the parliament’s committee on artificial intelligence has warned, ahead of federal inquiry hearings which will grill the tech company alongside Anthropic, Microsoft and Google.

Independent senator David Pocock is also demanding answers, saying OpenAI “still have a lot they need to answer” about their AI agent
title: OpenAI must explain action taken to stop AI hacking Australians’ private data, chair of federal inquiry says

author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
Former MP and Greens Institute head, Max Chandler-Mather, says proposal for publicly owned supermarket chain will ease grocery prices

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

More than 200 Coles and Woolworths supermarkets would be nationalised, and hundreds of government grocery stores opened, under a $25bn plan being put forward by former Greens MP Max Chandler-Mather.

Channelling New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s plan for publicly owned grocery stores, Chandler-Mather, the boss of the party’s thinktank, the Greens Institute, wants to use new forced divestiture laws to take over major supermarket sites and three distribution centres.
title: Greens pitch Zohran Mamdani-style $25.1bn plan to nationalise 200 Coles and Woolworths supermarkets

author: Edward Helmore
description:
Ryo Uchimiya was sleeping in his car waiting for his shift to begin when a 16-year-old crashed into him

A longtime chef for the famous Japanese restaurant chain Nobu was killed over the weekend in Malibu, California, when a teen driver crashed into his parked vehicle, where he was sleeping while waiting for his shift to start.

The 51-year-old chef, named by the Los Angeles medical examiner’s office as Ryo Uchimiya, had arrived at work at Nobu Malibu early on Saturday when his vehicle was hit by a 16-year-old boy driving a Range Rover at 6.50am.

Continue reading...
title: Nobu chef killed by teen driver who crashed into his parked car in Malibu

author: Adam Gabbatt
description:
Medical transport plane flying from Bermuda to Boston crashed off coast of Massachusetts early Saturday

Six people are presumed dead after the US Coast Guard on Sunday suspended its search for survivors of a medical transport plane crash off the coast of Massachusetts early the previous day.

The aircraft, which was flying from Bermuda to Boston, lost contact with ground authorities at about 2am on Saturday, and the Coast Guard located a debris field near the island of Nantucket later that day.

Continue reading...
title: Six presumed dead as Coast Guard suspends search for missing medical plane near Nantucket

author: Hilary Osborne
description:
Banks and building societies raise prices as turmoil in bond markets increases expectations of base rate rise

The average cost of a five-year fixed-rate mortgage has hit the 6% barrier for the first time in three years, as jitters in the money markets make the loans more expensive for lenders to offer.

Figures from financial information provider Moneyfacts show the average is now 6.00%, its highest point since September 2023, while the average two-year fixed rate is not far behind at 5.98%, its highest since December of the same year.

Continue reading...
title: Average five-year fixed mortgage rate hits 6% for first time in three years

author: Martin Belam
description:
Flávio Bolsonaro is favorite to win 25 October runoff against 80-year-old incumbent leftwing president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Plus the ‘pawsome’ new recruit to Mexico’s national guard

  • Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here

Good morning. Brazil’s presidential race will go to a second round after the far-right candidate, Flávio Bolsonaro, beat the incumbent leftwing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, but failed to secure the outright majority he needed to avoid a runoff.

The 45-year-old son of the disgraced former president Jair Bolsonaro will go into the second round as strong favourite, likely to pick up votes from the election’s other rightwing candidates, in
title: Son of disgraced ex-president Jair Bolsonaro takes election lead in Brazil | First Thing

author: Lauren Almeida
description:
German-owned supermarket beats Morrisons to become fifth largest grocer in Great Britain

  • Business live – latest updates

Lidl’s sales in Great Britain jumped 10% to more than £13bn this year, as shoppers sought out cheaper fresh meat, fruit and vegetables and snapped up its Deluxe range.

Pre-tax profit at the German-owned supermarket’s arm in Great Britain grew by 30% to £245.5m in the year ended in February, up from £156.8m in the previous year.

Continue reading...
title: Lidl GB’s sales soar by over 10%, helped by price cuts and Deluxe range

author: Adam Morton in Nadi, Fiji
description:
Anthony Albanese joins about 4,000 people in Fiji for preparatory meeting for year-ending Cop31 UN climate summit

  • Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here

The Australian prime minister, Anthony Albanese, has declared it is “important that Pacific voices are heard” after landing in Fiji on Monday to attend his first UN climate summit since becoming prime minister more than four years ago.

Albanese joined about 4,000 people in Nadi for a preparatory meeting for the year-ending Cop31 UN climate summit in Turkey while facing criticism from his political opponents at home. Pre-Cop meetings are usually small and bureaucratic affairs, but this meeting has a double purpose: it is being held in the Pacific after Australia and regional leaders argued it woul
title: Mixed start for pre-Cop as just two non-Pacific leaders accept Australian invitation to climate summit

author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
description:
Vivien Lichtenstein says she believes motion is unhelpful as anger grows over Zack Polanski’s absence for vote

The head of the Jewish Greens has said she may leave the party after it voted to adopt a policy that equates Zionism with racism and calls for Israel to be replaced by a single Palestinian state.

Vivien Lichtenstein said that while opinion among Jewish members of the party was split on the motion passed at its annual conference in Brighton on Sunday, she said she believed it was unhelpful and it was “possible” she might quit.

Continue reading...
title: Head of Jewish Greens says she may leave party over ‘Zionism is racism’ vote

author: Guardian staff and agency
description:
Mountbatten-Windsor to challenge whether Thames Valley police acted lawfully over searches that led to his arrest

Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor is taking legal action against Thames Valley police in an effort to quash search warrants that led to his arrest, with a private high court hearing to take place on Thursday, a judicial spokesperson has said.

The former Duke of York has been granted permission to challenge whether the force acted lawfully over the searches relating to his arrest in February. Andrew’s application for a judicial review is said to have been made earlier this year and recently approved by a high court judge.

Continue reading...
title: Andrew launches court action against police over Epstein raids

author: Andrew Sparrow
description:
Andrew Griffith makes speech today as Reform UK accuses party of copying policies they ‘announced weeks and months ago’

  • Tories to pledge to scrap Environment Agency and Natural England

Last night Israel’s foreign affairs ministry said that Zack Polanski, the Green party leader, has been banned from the country following his party conference voting for a motion saying “Zionism is racism”.

The motion was “a clear antisemitic text according to the IHRA definition, as it denies the Jewish people’s right to self-determination”, the ministry said. It went on:

Therefore, as a first step, foreign minister Gideon Sa’ar has decided this evening to declare Green party leader Zack Polanski barred from entering Israel.
title: Shadow chancellor to address Tory conference as he claims slashing red tape could cut cost of new houses by £50,000 – UK politics live

author: Sam Jones  and Ashifa Kassam in Madrid
description:
Election called after rightwing parties voted down emergency legislation aimed at tackling housing crisis

Spain’s socialist prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, has announced a snap general election three days after rightwing parties torpedoed the emergency legislation his minority government had put forward in response to growing public anger over the country’s housing crisis.

Sánchez, who has been in office since 2018, used a televised address on Monday morning to communicate his decision, which had been widely expected.

Continue reading...
title: Spain’s PM Pedro Sánchez calls snap election after housing legislation fails to pass

author: Chris Osuh
description:
Percentage who feel ‘very emotionally attached to Israel’ rose to 51% in June 2025, up 13 points from before Gaza war

British Jews have become more likely to identify as Zionist, consider emigrating to Israel, and feel a close attachment to the country since the 7 October attacks, research has found.

A study from the Institute for Jewish Policy Research (JPR) titled “October 8 Jews: The Impact of October 7 on British Jewish Identity”, by Dr David Graham, found the percentage of British Jews who identified as Zionist rose seven points to 66%, between 2022 and 2025. By June 2025, the numbers who felt antisemitism in the UK was a “very big problem” had tripled to 50%.

Continue reading...
title: British Jews more likely to identify as Zionist since 7 October attacks, research finds

author: Graham Readfearn Environment and climate correspondent
description:
Alpine areas also experience record-breaking heat with snow depth recorded at zero in Kosciuszko national park

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia had its second hottest September on record last month as global heating and a strengthening El Niño combined to break a string of heat records around the country.

Bureau of Meteorology data showed the minimum night-time temperatures across the continent were also the hottest for any September on a record that goes back to 1910. Averaged temperatures ranked in the top five warmest Septembers for every state, and the sixth hottest for the Northern Territory.
title: Australia experiences second hottest September on record as El Niño and climate crisis combine

author: Nino Bucci and Adeshola Ore
description:
RMIT confirms co-pilot was a student as Australian authorities examine his time in country between 2015 and 2017

An Australian university has confirmed a flydubai co-pilot who allegedly tried to hijack an Israel-bound flight studied at its Melbourne campus, but left before completing his qualification.

Disaster was narrowly averted on 30 September when passengers and crew intervened to stop the alleged attempt of the co-pilot, identified by media outlets as Hammam al-Hammami, to take control of a flight to Tel Aviv with 182 people onboard.

Continue reading...
title: Alleged flydubai attacker left Australia without finishing engineering course, university says

author: Libby Brooks
description:
In today’s newsletter: As Americans get ready to vote on whether the Republican party remains in control of Congress, our Washington editor talks about the disconnect between Trump and his supporters

Good morning. Later today, Donald Trump will be in the state of Nebraska to rev up supporters as he kicks off a campaign blitz of rallies ahead of the midterm elections on 3 November.

If his early speeches are anything to go by, cornhuskers can anticipate poll denial, accusations of veganism and an expletive ratio that my nine-year-old would love. And Nebraskans may love it, too: aside from one “blue dot” district in Omaha, Republicans argue their support is steady in the state that has easily backed Trump three times.

UK politics | The Greens in England and Wales have
title: Monday briefing: You asked, we answered – how will the US midterms go?

author: Petra Stock
description:
Juvenile humpback was spotted near Bundjalung national park in what experts say is a rare but not unprecedented event

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

While the case of a whale found 11km upstream in a New South Wales river this weekend was unusual, it was not unprecedented, experts say.

The juvenile humpback, which swam into the Clarence River on the state’s mid-north coast and later died, was towed out to sea on Sunday, according to NSW authorities.

Continue reading...
title: Authorities issue shark warning over whale that swam 11km upstream in Clarence River and later died

author: Stephanie Convery and AAP
description:
Officers were responding to reports a car had driven into a tree 84km north of Yass on Sunday

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A man has been shot dead by police in regional New South Wales after allegedly aiming a loaded rifle at officers responding to a car crash.

NSW police were responding to reports that a car had driven into a tree on a road 84km north of Yass about 2.50pm on Sunday.

Continue reading...
title: Man shot dead after crashing car and allegedly pointing gun at NSW police

author: Sarah Basford Canales
description:
Barnaby Joyce defends move, saying party will lease space from mining billionaire’s company at commercial rates

  • One Nation celebrated stunning success in Queensland in 1998 – then it all fell apart. What happened?

  • Listen to episode 4 of The Populist podcast

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Barnaby Joyce says there’s no conflict of interest between One Nation and the mining billionaire Gina Rinehart after it was revealed that Australia
title: One Nation to establish headquarters in multimillion-dollar Brisbane office bought by Gina Rinehart

author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
The announcement came hours after Iranian-backed Houthis reportedly cut a vital supply route to besieged city of Taiz

Yemen’s Saudi-backed government has announced the start of a new military operation to retake all territory held by the Houthis, even as the militant group made fresh gains on the ground, reportedly encircling a government-held city.

Rashad al-Alimi, the head of Yemen’s presidential council, said in a statement on Sunday: “I announce today the start of military operations to retake the remaining territories of the republic and extend the authority of the state and its institutions across the entire national territory.”

Continue reading...
title: Yemen’s Saudi-backed government launches military drive to retake all Houthi-held territory
